text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 - GPU OOM observed on decode-worker-7 for service=streaming-svc. Pager triggered. Logs: cudaErrorIllegalAddress + container restart. Please ack and join #incidents.
sara: acked. seeing repeated "OOM when allocating" in decode logs, node flapped at 1718001242.
jake: I'm oncall - looking. any customer impact yet?
amanda: CS ticket created — customer reported ~30% request failures since 11:20 UTC. escalation flagged. ID #C-8342.
mei: quick telemetry: upstream burst with long max_tokens headers from a single api-key. token distribution skewed: median 150, tail 5k+. host-level mem spike lines attached to thread.
liam: If tail requests are unbounded they fill KV cache and decode allocs -> OOM. Need to throttle or enforce hard cap at ingress ASAP.
sara: can we hotpatch the gateway to reject requests with header "X-Client-Max-Tokens" > 2048? currently service default max is 1024 but header override allowed.
jake: pushing kill-switch middleware to reject >1024. doing canary to 10% traffic on region us-west-2.
deploy-bot: deploy started by jake: deploy/ingress-throttle v2026.03.17-rc1 -> canary us-west-2 (10%).
mei: logs during canary: decode-worker-7 still OOM'd once, likely existing pods with hot KV cache. we should evict those pods to reclaim GPU mem.
liam: +1 evicting nodes. running: `kubectl delete pod decode-worker-7 -n streaming --grace-period=0 --force` on two nodes.
amanda: customer update draft: "We're investigating elevated failures; temporary traffic cap applied to large requests; we're rolling a mitigation and will follow up in 30m." sending now.
cust-success: customer on standby for bridge. they asked if this is a regression - any config changes? they noted no change on their side.
sara: root cause looks like client-side misconfig / attack vector: a batch job started sending long generations (max_tokens header set to 5000) after a deployment of their client. we should confirm and recommend backpressure.
jake: mitigation status: canary OK (0 hits >1024 now), global rollouts queued. initiating pod evictions and model-scale fallback (route to smaller model `gpt-lite` for offending key) to reduce per-token memory.
mei: applied quick rule: route api-key XZ-*** to gpt-lite and set hard token cap 512. verifying.
liam: nodes drained and restarted; decode-worker pods come back healthy. no further OOMs in last 4 minutes.
amanda: updated customer message: "Mitigation deployed: large-request caps and temporary model downgrade for your traffic. We're monitoring; please confirm if you see improved success rate." sent.
cust-success: customer confirms lower error rate, appreciates proactive routing. asked for postmortem and ask for quota recommendations.
sara: root-cause timeline for postmortem: client-side header allowed >app-config limit (bug in client v2.4.1) -> token storm -> KV growth -> GPU alloc exhaustion -> container restarts -> request drops. detection delayed because our telemetry aggregated tokens but didn't trigger tail alert.
jake: action items:
- emergency: enforce ingress hard cap 1024 (prod) and make canary permanent -> DONE
- medium: add tail-token-rate alert + per-key token percentile telemetry -> OWNER: mei
- medium: automatic per-key fallback to smaller model on repeated heavy requests -> OWNER: liam
- long: update docs + client SDK to sanitize max_tokens -> OWNER: sara
mei: rolling a follow-up alert rule now. will propose thresholds in 2 hours.
deploy-bot: deploy complete: ingress-throttle v2026.03.17 -> prod
jake: handing off to daytime oncall @mei for monitoring; I'll stay available for customer calls.
incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated. P2 -> monitoring. incident channel will remain open for postmortem notes.
amanda: CS will schedule a 1:1 briefing with customer and send apology + timeline. CS will include recommended quota changes.
cust-success: please ping when postmortem posted. closing the support bridge in 60m if stable.
sara: noted. collecting logs and patch diff. will author postmortem draft tonight.
jake: thanks team :thumbsup: good recovery.
